verdicts.reason: The gap is real. D-3's next list (data/visamap.yaml:248-253) is exactly D-10-1, D-2-2 (abroad), E-7-1 (abroad) and E-9 (abroad), with no family route. Two parts of the finding are wrong, though. First, it is not true that every other status offers F-6-1: H-2 does not, and neither do 37 other non-F-5 nodes, including D-8-*, D-9-*, E-8, D-4-3, D-4-6 and D-10-2/3/T. Second, the in-Korea F-6-1 change is barred only for short-term visas, overstayers, people given extra time to leave, and criminal offenders, and D-3 is not on that list. The D-3 chapter's '불가 원칙' is about changing into D-3 (visadocs-targets: 'D-3: abroad,extend'). So `abroad: true` has no support, and the edge should be an ordinary in-Korea change like the E-9 and E-10 edges. F-2-3 belongs with it because in this file F-6-1 and F-2-3 always come as a pair (the same 46 origins), even though F-2-3 is about the spouse of a permanent resident, not of a Korean citizen.

verdicts.reason: The graph part is mostly right: D-8-2 and D-8-3 are reached only from NONE, so from abroad only. The headline is wrong for D-8-1, which D-7 already offers as an in-Korea change (plain `- D-8-1`), so D-8-4 is not the only D-8 a resident can be shown. On the law, a Ministry of Justice D-8 guideline notice restricts an in-Korea change to D-8-1/D-8-3 only for D-3, E-9, E-10 and G-1 holders (and short-term tourists). D-2, D-10, E-7 and D-9 holders are not restricted, and the change document lists for D-8-1/2/3 carry no condition on the status held before. The D-10-2 -> D-8-2 part of the fix is not supported: D-10-2 is the start-up preparation track for D-8 다목 (tech start-up, which is D-8-4), and D-10-2 -> D-8-4 is already in the file.

verdicts.reason: Correct as stated. In the current YAML, F-5-5 is reached from D-8-1, D-8-2, D-8-3, F-2-5 and NONE, but not from D-8-4. 별표 1의3 제3호 sets no condition on the status held, and the F-5 manual says large investors may apply whatever their period of residence; NONE -> F-5-5 already treats the route as status-free. The finding's reasoning is off in one way: F-5-5 needs the applicant personally to be the foreign investor (FIPA) who put in US$500K, not a founder who raised that money; such founders are served by F-5-24, already on D-8-4. That does not affect the fix. F-5-5 has a change list, and its `needs: {invest: 3}` gates it.

verdicts.reason: The rule is right: the manual's D-2-5 row requires a master's degree in principle, and the only undergraduate opening is for STEM students enrolled in a bachelor's programme abroad who are invited by a Korean university in the QS top 500 or THE top 200. But 'regardless of education' is wrong, and the fix does nothing. readDetails (visamap.js:237-241) forces stem=false unless edu>=1. I reproduced it: edu 0 + STEM is already 'no'; edu 1 + STEM is 'yes' both with and without `{stem: true, edu: 1}`; blank edu is 'maybe' both ways. The engine has no way to say 'currently enrolled' or 'invited by a ranked Korean university' (rank is the reader's own university). So keep the needs and put the real conditions in the text.

Master's degree or higher in principle; a STEM student still enrolled in a bachelor's programme abroad qualifies only when invited by a Korean university in the QS top 500 or THE top 200.' The ru, uz and uz-cyrl texts must be translated from this.

verdicts.reason: The engine part is right: `age: [0, 19]` on D-4-3 is a hard gate (visamap.js:176-182). The D-4-3 change, abroad and extend document lists (visadocs.yaml:5288-5385) contain no age item; they gate on the school, the admission letter and a guardian bond (후견보증서), with a waiver for dormitory residents. But no source gives any other age limit, so 21 (or no limit) is as unsourced as 19. The guardian requirement and immigration guidance describe D-4-3 as a study visa for minors (미성년자; adulthood in Korea is 19). Dropping the gate would show a K-12 visa as open to adults. The claim that 19-20-year-olds commonly enrol is uncited, and the primary manuals could not be fetched here.
